lines.text: My name is Jira. I'm nine. I keep a notebook of every strange thing my family has ever done, and until this summer it was a very boring notebook.
I'm Joel. I'm seven. One time I sneezed into a pond and the pond respected me after that.
This year we are visiting Grandma, the mountains, the caves, a storybook, a science museum, a light dome, and a museum. In one trip. Because I am an optimist.
We are visiting Grandma. The rest is negotiable. Nobody is asking the children for directions.
But the scrapbook was already full. Seven pages, every single one our vacation, dated before we left. And every page had a little empty corner, like someone had been standing just outside the photo.
And when I looked at the corner, something little looked back. Then it moved the tornado.
So now the vacations are bigger, and stranger, and there are clues everywhere. All we have to do is survive them. And find whoever keeps taking the pictures.

ending.kicker: The last page of the scrapbook
ending.title: One Small Shadow

lines.text: You came back. Every year you come back, and every year I keep the day safe, and every year you forget it a little faster.
You weren't stealing them. You were keeping them. That's not the same thing at all.
You can come with us, you know. There's a cupholder. I've measured it.
I do not fit in a cupholder. I have never been in a photograph. I am mostly made of the corners.
Then stand in the middle for once. One photo. All of us. Jira, move your brother. Joel, stop licking the camera.
Everybody say 'this was the weirdest vacation ever'.
THIS WAS THE WEIRDEST VACATION EVER.
The photo developed with five of us in it. Four in the front, one very small shadow in the corner, smiling so hard it was practically glowing.
The scrapbook has a new page now. It's blank. Dad already wrote the dates on it. Next summer, apparently.
Jacquelyn — practical, smart, quick-witted, usually correct, always the one holding the map upside down on purpose.
Jordan — optimistic, enthusiastic, and responsible for escalating every single one of these vacations.
Nine. Brave, curious, dramatic storyteller, and the only one who writes any of this down.
Seven. Funny, impulsive, accident-prone, endless enthusiasm. Fits in ducts.
Keeps the afternoons. Would like to be in the photo. Has been asked now.
